_doc: Graymourne, the fog-bound port (the user's spec of 2026-11-07, docs/graymourne.txt): its people and quests. 896 writes them into the brokenspire level's generator as townsfolk and quests of the town "Graymourne" (FRDTownsfolkDef::Town, FRDQuestDef::Town): a role it has people for takes those in its posts (RDTownPlan.cpp's port), the others the shared ones. The functional ones: the harbourmaster (the Elder's part: talk, quests), the coroner (the Scholar's), the watch captain (the Captain's), the trades' keepers (their services). The quests count the sewers' own counters ("sewers:enter", ":tier", ":kills", ":boss").

townsfolk.name: GM_Harbourmaster
townsfolk.title: Harbourmaster Edda Strand
townsfolk.calling: who keeps the port's books and its dead
lines: Mind the edge of the quay. The fog hides it, and the water does not give back what it takes. Most days.
Three ships this month. Forty-one bodies. Write that in your ledger and see how it reads.
topics: Where do the bodies come from?|The tide brings them in every morning, more than ever drowned off this coast. Old sailors, new sailors, men lost a century ago. They come up the outfalls first.
What is under the town?|The sewers. Built by the founders, deepened by every harbourmaster since, and now nobody goes past the first sluice. The dead come up that way. The tide only finishes the job.
How do I get down?|The Sluice House, in the middle of town. Behind its far wall is the old grate. It opens for anyone foolish enough.

townsfolk.name: GM_Coroner
townsfolk.title: Coroner Thaddeus Pell
townsfolk.calling: who counts and names the drowned
lines: I have a name for one in three. The rest I describe. A hat, a tattoo, a ring nobody claims.
Do not touch them with bare hands. Some of them are not finished drowning.
topics: What do the dead tell you?|That they drowned in the sewers, not the sea. Fresh water in the lungs, every one. Something down there is drowning men and sending them out to sea.
How deep are the sewers?|Five levels, the plans say, each below the last. The bottom one was a cistern once. The plans call it the Mere. I do not know what it is now.

townsfolk.name: GM_Captain
townsfolk.title: Watch-Captain Bram Hollow
lines: My watch walks the quay with lanterns and hooks. The lanterns are for the fog. The hooks are for what climbs out of the water.
If you go down, take a light. And a second one.
topics: What comes up out of the sewers?|The drowned. They walk, at night, up the outfalls and along the quay. My men put them back down. Every night there are more.
How do I help?|Thin them out below, before they reach the outfalls. And whatever drives them, find it.

townsfolk.name: GM_Priest
townsfolk.title: Mother Wren of the Tides
lines: We sing for the drowned every dawn. Lately the choir has not been large enough.
A blessing keeps the cold out of your lungs. For a while.

townsfolk.name: GM_Smith
townsfolk.title: Osric Tarr
lines: Salt eats steel. Bring it to me before it eats yours through.
Anchors, hooks, chains. And now swords. The swords sell best.

townsfolk.name: GM_Trader
townsfolk.title: Mags Fennick
lines: Rope, tar, lamp oil, potions. Whatever the fog has not ruined.
The ships do not come in like they did. Buy while I still have stock.

townsfolk.name: GM_Healer
townsfolk.title: Sister Morwenna
lines: Cough it up. All of it. Good. Now the next lungful.
The ones that come back from the sewers cough black water for days.

townsfolk.name: GM_Keeper
townsfolk.title: Old Gull
lines: Leave it with me. The customs house has kept cargo dry for two hundred years.

townsfolk.name: GM_Innkeeper
townsfolk.title: Rosamund Brine
lines: Warm rum and a seat by the fire. Nobody sits by the window any more.
The fog came in a year ago and has not gone out since. Neither have my regulars.

townsfolk.name: GM_Preacher
townsfolk.title: Brother Ebb
lines: The sea gives back what we owe it! Every soul we ever sent down!
Repent before the tide comes in. It comes in twice a day.

townsfolk.name: GM_Sailor1
townsfolk.title: a sailor
townsfolk.calling: of a ship that will not sail
lines: Captain says we sail when the fog lifts. The fog does not lift.
I saw my brother on the quay this morning. They buried him at sea in the spring.

townsfolk.name: GM_Sailor2
townsfolk.title: a sailor
townsfolk.calling: of a ship that will not sail
lines: Hold your breath when you pass the outfalls. Trust me.
We came in for water and a refit. That was three months ago.

townsfolk.name: GM_Sailor3
townsfolk.title: a sailor
townsfolk.calling: of a ship that will not sail
lines: You hear them at night, under the piers. Knocking.

townsfolk.name: GM_Dockhand1
townsfolk.title: a dockhand
lines: Crates in, crates out. Fewer in every week.
Mind your feet. The planks are slick with fog.

townsfolk.name: GM_Dockhand2
townsfolk.title: a dockhand
lines: We stack the bodies by the warehouses till the coroner comes. Nobody pays us for that.

townsfolk.name: GM_Fisher1
townsfolk.title: a fisherwoman
lines: The nets come up full. Not always with fish.
Buy a herring? They are fresh. The fog keeps them cold.

townsfolk.name: GM_Fisher2
townsfolk.title: a fisherman
lines: Mended the same net four times this week. Something keeps tearing through it from below.

townsfolk.name: GM_Mourner1
townsfolk.title: a widow on the quay
lines: I look at every one they bring in. One day it will be him.
He went down the sluice to fetch his net. A net.

townsfolk.name: GM_Mourner2
townsfolk.title: a mourner
lines: Close their eyes. They stare at the fog if you do not.

townsfolk.name: GM_Guard1
townsfolk.title: a harbour watchman
lines: Welcome to Graymourne. Keep to the lamplight.
The harbour is that way. Follow the gulls. If you can hear any.

townsfolk.name: GM_Guard2
townsfolk.title: a harbour watchman
lines: The Sluice House stays shut at night. Mostly.

townsfolk.name: GM_Militia1
townsfolk.title: a watchman on the walls
lines: You cannot see the sea from the sea wall any more. Only hear it.

townsfolk.name: GM_Militia2
townsfolk.title: a watchman on the walls
lines: Fog again. Fog tomorrow too.

townsfolk.name: GM_Soldier1
townsfolk.title: a soldier of the watch
lines: Hook them under the arms and push them back in. That is the drill.

townsfolk.name: GM_Soldier2
townsfolk.title: a soldier of the watch
lines: They do not bleed. They leak.

townsfolk.name: GM_Child1
townsfolk.title: Pike
lines: I found a ring on one of them! Mum made me throw it back.
Are you going in the sewers? Bring me a crab. A big one.

townsfolk.name: GM_Child2
townsfolk.title: Minnow
lines: I can hold my breath for a whole minute! Watch!

townsfolk.name: GM_Idiot
townsfolk.title: Drip-Drip Dorran
lines: Drip, drip, drip. That is them talking. Drip, drip, they are saying come down.
The Mere is rising! Rising, rising!

townsfolk.name: GM_Citizen1
townsfolk.title: a citizen
lines: Good day. Or night. Hard to tell under all this fog.
Keep your shutters closed. Everyone does now.

townsfolk.name: GM_Citizen2
townsfolk.title: a citizen
lines: Half the houses on our street are boarded. Their people moved inland. Or into the harbour.

townsfolk.name: GM_Citizen3
townsfolk.title: a citizen
lines: Another sword. Good. The watch needs every one it can borrow.

quests.title: Down the Old Grate
quests.offer: Behind the Sluice House's far wall is the old grate down into the sewers. Go down, see where the dead are coming from, and come back up to tell me.
quests.done: You came back up dry. Mostly. That is more than the last three managed.
quests.hint: Go down through the grate in the Sluice House

quests.title: Open the Second Sluice
quests.offer: The second level's sluices have been shut since the fog came. Open the way to the second level, and the water might run clean again.
quests.done: The drains ran this morning. Black, but they ran. Thank you.

quests.title: What the Tide Brings
quests.offer: The coroner says the drowned come from the deepest levels, near the old cistern. Reach the fourth level, and the stair beyond it.
quests.done: So deep. If the Mere is the heart of it, you are knocking on its door.

quests.title: Drowned Men Walking
quests.offer: Every one you put down below is one my watch does not hook off the quay at dawn. Twenty-five.
quests.done: Twenty-five. The quay was quiet this morning. First time in a month.

quests.title: The Sluice Warden
quests.offer: Something rules each level down there. My men have seen one: it drags the others behind it. Kill one of those.
quests.done: One of the big ones. My watch will drink to you, and then they will lock the Sluice House again.
quests.hint: Kill a level's warden in the sewers

quests.title: Name the Dead
quests.offer: The widows on the quay know the faces I do not. Speak to one of them; ask who she has seen come in with the tide.
quests.done: Men forty years drowned, she says. Then it is the old dead too. I will write that down.
quests.hint: Speak to a mourner on the quay

quests.title: Bounty: The Outfall Rats
quests.offer: The fishmongers' guild pays for every thing killed below the outfalls. Ten of them, twenty-five coins.
quests.done: The fishmongers pay, holding their noses.
